codeReview.summary: Commit 3b521f5 implements the required Oracle Linux 10 arm64 UEK package mapping and adds a pre-kernel repo-enable stage, while preserving existing Fedora/RHEL-family behavior via distro-specific kernel-package precedence and targeted regression tests.

issues.description: The UEK repo enable command uses `dnf config-manager --enable ol10_UEKR8 || true`, which suppresses enablement failures. Kernel install will still fail later if the repo is not enabled, but this stage no longer guarantees immediate failure on repo-enable errors.

sharedStateObservations.observation: Feature metadata declares `skillName` as `runtime-worker`, but the expected in-repo procedure file is not present, limiting direct procedure-auditability from repository state.
sharedStateObservations.evidence: `features.json` for feature `oracle10-arm64-kernel-package-mapping-fix` sets `skillName` to `runtime-worker`; `/home/sandbox/kairos-init/.factory/skills/runtime-worker` exists but is empty (no `SKILL.md`).

sharedStateObservations.observation: Repository-level service/command manifest is missing, so canonical mission command discovery is not available from shared state.
sharedStateObservations.evidence: Read of `/home/sandbox/kairos-init/.factory/services.yaml` returned ENOENT, and glob search under `/home/sandbox` found no `services.yaml` file.

summary: Review complete: the feature behavior is functionally correct for Oracle arm64 UEK kernel resolution and includes good regression coverage; one non-blocking robustness concern was noted around suppressed repo-enable command failures.
